key_insight: A data-driven algorithm can automatically detect multiscale self-similarity in turbulence and recover both classical scaling laws and their corrections directly from numerical data.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical, equation-agnostic tool for discovering inner/outer scaling regimes and transition laws in turbulent flows, which can improve modeling and interpretation of multiscale engineering systems.
method: Extends prior single-scale self-similarity identification to multiscale settings
Applies the algorithm to channel flow and decaying turbulence data
Extracts similarity expressions and associated scaling laws from different flow regions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful recovery of inner and outer similarity in two canonical problems, plus the logarithmic law and -5/3 law in intermediate regions, with additional corrections.
watch_item: The approach appears to rely on high-quality numerical data and careful regime separation, so performance on noisy experimental data or ambiguous scale overlap may be challenging.
paper_title: Data-driven identification of multiscale self-similarity and asymptotic matching
